doc.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995

chapter: The late-1950s Basie band and closing
title: Papa Foss song and nickname
summary: Foster explains the song Papa Foss written by Danny Mixon and sung by Carmen Bradford.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: were playing, but they weren’t old cats. Those were young cats playing the music of their time.
What’s this thing about Papa Foss? I heard that song the other day.

That’s what the thing about Papa— it’s a pianist by the name of Danny Mixon who played with me in my small group and he’s a Loud Minority so you know he’s Spacetakovitch, like we all were, and he composed this song called “Papa Foss” [scats]. So he didn’t have any lyrics to it. So my wife Cecelia and I got together and we put the lyrics to this song. and I sold Carmen Bradford on the idea of singing it. And of course it put me out front, you know, “standing out in front of it is Papa Foss, been out in front of it is Papa Foss.” So it showed me off in a very good light. So and I was very happy that she agreed to sing it. And we got recorded, and it’s in the annals so to speak.
Yeah, they’ve been playing it in Syracuse.
Yeah, they’ve got a good jazz station there.

Well that’s good to know. We don’t play it anymore now that Carmen’s not with the band, because that was her song, I mean, she put something on it that I don’t think anyone else could. And of course we had a trumpet battle between Bob Ojeda and the very brilliant Melton Mustafa, and they just took it to great levels.
Yeah it was something else. But people don’t call me that too much anymore. Thankfully. I’ll just be happy to be called “Foss.”
